# @ttoss/fsl-ui

Semantic, token-native React component library. Built on React Aria
Components; styled exclusively with `@ttoss/fsl-theme` CSS-variable tokens.
Every component declares a formal semantic identity (FSL — Foundational
Semantic Language) that determines which tokens it may consume.

Ground truth in the published package: `src/tokens/CONTRACT.md` (full Layer-2
contract). This file is the distilled, machine-oriented summary.

## Setup

```tsx
import { createTheme } from '@ttoss/fsl-theme';
import { ThemeProvider } from '@ttoss/fsl-theme/react';
import { Button } from '@ttoss/fsl-ui';

const theme = createTheme(); // base theme + dark alternate

<ThemeProvider theme={theme} defaultMode="system">
  <Button evaluation="primary" onPress={save}>Save</Button>
</ThemeProvider>
```

Without a ThemeProvider (or ThemeHead/ThemeScript on SSR) the CSS variables
are undefined and components render unstyled.

## Semantic model (what the props mean)

- entity — what the component IS (fixed per component, not a prop):
  Action, Input, Selection, Navigation, Disclosure, Overlay, Feedback,
  Collection, Structure.
- evaluation (prop) — AUTHORIAL emphasis, chosen when writing the UI:
  e.g. 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'accent' | 'muted' | 'negative' on Action.
  Input/Selection components have NO evaluation prop (data entry carries no
  authorial voice); validation is the runtime `invalid` STATE (`isInvalid`),
  never `evaluation="negative"`.
- consequence (prop) — effect on state: 'neutral' | 'committing' |
  'destructive'. Drives MECHANISM (e.g. ConfirmationDialog two-click arming),
  not color. Destructive ≠ negative color; pair them explicitly if desired.
- composition (prop on leaves) — slot the element plays inside a parent:
  'primaryAction' | 'secondaryAction' | 'dismissAction' … DialogActions
  reorders children by it per platform convention.
- State — runtime only (hover, active, focused, disabled, checked,
  indeterminate, expanded, invalid, …). Emitted by React Aria render props;
  priority cascade: disabled > invalid > expanded > indeterminate >
  selected > focusVisible > pressed > hovered > default.

## Component catalog (all exports also ship a `*Meta` identity object)

Action:      Button = COMMAND silhouette (commit: submit/confirm/primary action
             of a surface; pill radius, semibold, 40px desktop).
             ActionButton = UTILITY silhouette (ambient operation ON content:
             toolbar, row action, overflow trigger; control radius, label type,
             THE FIELD ROW — the same tokens TextField/Select resolve, not a
             pixel: the row's height is fluid because inset.control is
             container-fluid while sizing.hit is rem-anchored, measured
             32/32.5/34/34px at 390/900/1280/1920 (F-035). Pick by the
             weight of the commitment — there is no size prop, the pair IS the
             distinction. The two type contracts share one font SIZE and differ
             in WEIGHT only; a utility trigger is never independently smaller,
             or it desynchronises from the fields beside it.
             Both: icon={<Icon intent="…"/>} + iconPlacement=leading|trailing;
             omit children for the icon-only square (same height as the
             labelled form; aria-label then REQUIRED by the type system);
             anatomy data-part root|icon|label.
             ToggleButton = utility silhouette + persistent `pressed` state
             (aria-pressed; strong inverted fill when engaged).
             FileTrigger (opens OS file picker), MenuItem (inside Menu),
             FormSubmit (inside Form)
Navigation:  Link, Breadcrumbs/Breadcrumb, Tabs/TabList/Tab
             (TabPanel is Structure — the content revealed by the tabs)
Disclosure:  Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionPanel,
             Disclosure, DisclosureTrigger, DisclosurePanel (standalone single
             section — Accordion is the DisclosureGroup)
Selection:   Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup/Radio, Switch,
             Select/SelectItem, ToggleButtonGroup, TagGroup/Tag
             (Checkbox takes description + errorMessage for the confirmation
             shape ("I have read the terms"): the row becomes a 2-column grid,
             the accessible NAME stays the label alone (pinned via
             aria-labelledby — supporting copy placed in the row otherwise gets
             absorbed into the name), and the message shows only while invalid.
             A lone required Checkbox in a Form blocks submit; Switch has no
             message part yet (F-033).
             CheckboxGroup group-level isInvalid propagates to child Checkboxes.
             Select, CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup all take label/description/
             errorMessage: their label part is Selection/label, but description
             and validationMessage are INTERNAL parts — Selection has no such
             structural roles (they belong to Input), so they carry no meta and
             claim no legality. All three are addressable as
             [data-scope=…][data-part=validationMessage] regardless.
             Select also takes placeholder (shown until something is picked).
             A required Select blocks its Form's submit and focus returns to the
             TRIGGER: RAC submits the value through a visually hidden
             <select required>, which is also what onInvalid reports as its
             target — the one field whose event target is not the element
             carrying data-part="control".
             TagGroup/Tag: a chosen tag uses the `selected` State, NOT `pressed`
             — a tag is set membership, not a toggle; remove button is an
             internal closeTrigger part (not a Selection role))
Collection:  ListBox/ListBoxItem, GridList/GridListItem (+ Menu/MenuItem,
             listed under Overlay for its popover surface). ADR-007: the
             CONTAINER is Collection (informational surface) but selectable
             ITEMS are Selection (input chrome, `selected` State) — one
             composite, two entities. GridListItem also has a selectionControl
             (per-row checkbox).
             Table/TableHeader/TableColumn/TableBody/TableRow/TableCell —
             data table with columnheaders, same ADR-007 split (Table =
             Collection surface, TableRow = Selection). Sorting: controlled
             sortDescriptor/onSortChange + allowsSorting on TableColumn
             (aria-sort + direction arrow rendered for you); set isRowHeader
             on the naming column. Selection: selectionMode single|multiple,
             row click toggles (no checkbox column yet). Use for column-
             aligned data; GridList is for single-column rows.
THE FIELD ENVELOPE — one rule for every field, Input and Selection alike:
             root ▸ label ▸ control ▸ description ▸ validationMessage. An invalid
             field spans TWO token lines and this is the one place a part reads a
             role other than its component's: the CONTROL keeps the role it was
             authored with and flips that role's `invalid` state (a `muted` field
             that fails is still `muted` — re-voicing it as evaluation="negative"
             is the category mistake FSL Lexicon §10.15 names), while the
             VALIDATION MESSAGE reads input.negative.text.* because it is the part
             *reporting* the outcome. The control's `invalid` ink is its ordinary
             reading ink on purpose; the valence on the control is the border
             alone. HOVER DOES NOT APPLY WHILE INVALID (owner ruling) — `invalid`
             outranks `hover` in the cascade and `border` never reads hover at
             all; focus is unaffected because the ring is a separate declaration. The label
             carries the necessity marker when the field isRequired: an
             aria-hidden asterisk, because the control already carries the native
             `required` attribute and a second announcement is noise. Turn it off
             for a whole form with <Form necessityIndicator="none"> — the field
             stays required either way. LABEL PLACEMENT is the same kind of
             decision: <Form labelPosition="side"> puts every label in ONE column
             shared by the whole form (grid subgrid), so all controls start at the
             same x — which is why it is a Form prop and not a field prop, and why
             it only pays off on a wide multi-row form. Checkbox and Switch keep
             their inline label but still take the control column.
             Host knob: --fsl-form-label-width (default max-content).
             The message part is always mounted, so
             omitting errorMessage shows the platform's own localized constraint
             copy. Two exceptions, each with its mechanism: a lone Checkbox or
             Switch renders its copy inline inside its own <label> (which is why
             the accessible name is pinned via aria-labelledby), and Switch has no
             validation props at all in RAC (F-033); Slider gets no
             FieldErrorContext, because a slider always holds an in-range value.
Input:       TextField, TextArea — each authored EITHER one-line
             (label/description/errorMessage/placeholder props) OR by composing
             its slots (Label/Control/Description/Error). The two are mutually
             exclusive by type: passing copy props AND children is a compile
             error, not a precedence rule. Prefer one-line; reach for slots when
             the arrangement is unusual. In the one-line form the message slot
             is always mounted, so a field with no errorMessage still shows the
             platform's own constraint copy (already localized) — which is the
             better default for isRequired and type="email".
             SearchField (label/description/errorMessage/placeholder props OR
             + Label/Control slots; leading search + clear glyphs; clearLabel is
             required and caller-localized),
             NumberField (label/description/errorMessage props + −/+ steppers),
             Slider (label + value output; single value or [min,max] range),
             ComboBox/ComboBoxItem (text input + typeahead-filtered list;
             label/description/errorMessage/placeholder/triggerLabel props).
             THREE SPLIT CONTROLS — ComboBox, NumberField, SearchField:
             data-part="frame" paints the box and hosts the adornments,
             data-part="control" is the <input> you operate. `control` ALWAYS
             names the operated element, so a test or an agent told to type into
             a field can (ADR-022). SearchField and NumberField used to name both
             `control` (F-026, closed in forms item D) — querySelector returned
             the wrapper, which reported none of the field's chrome.
             AN EMBEDDED TRIGGER — the clear button, the steppers, the chevron —
             is one silhouette (EMBEDDED_TRIGGER, contract invariant #14): a
             `hit`-square box with `inset.control.sm` around a `sizing.icon.sm`
             glyph. Two traps it exists for: it must DECLARE the row's type,
             because a <button> with no type inherits the UA's 13.3333px and any
             font-relative glyph inside it shrinks (`Icon size="text"` did — the
             chevron came out 25.33px while its siblings were 32 and 20); and its
             colours come from the HOST, not from action.*, because the
             entity→ux-context test binds colour reads to a file's declared
             entities. Its box is `hit` and not the glyph's 20px because WCAG
             2.5.8 wants 24px targets and adjacent steppers cannot use the
             spacing exception.
             SearchField's clear button renders ONLY when there is a value. React
             Aria publishes emptiness as data-empty for CSS and this package ships
             none, so it is gated on the root's isEmpty render prop.
             ALL THREE embedded triggers are tabindex="-1" (measured) — React Aria
             keeps them out of the tab order, because the input is the tab stop
             and owns the keys (arrows step a NumberField; Escape clears a
             SearchField). Do not write a test that Tabs to a stepper or a clear
             button; click it, or drive the input.
             A PICKER'S POPOVER TAKES THE FIELD'S WIDTH (Select + ComboBox,
             ADR-023): min-width is the trigger's width unconditionally, width
             defaults to it and is widenable per host via
             --fsl-select-popover-width / --fsl-combo-box-popover-width. Options
             longer than the field WRAP; they do not widen the list. A MENU IS
             NOT A PICKER — Menu and Popover size to their own content and keep
             --fsl-menu-min-width / --fsl-popover-max-width.
             THE CHOOSABLE ROW IS ONE DECISION (Select/ComboBox options, MenuItem,
             ListBoxItem, GridListItem): 32px = the field row's content box, the
             same insets/radius/type as the field, `hit` as the ergonomic floor,
             and the focus ring INSET by the ring's own width because every such
             row sits in a clipped or scrolling surface. Never tune a row per
             component — it comes from CHOOSABLE_ROW.
             Pick ComboBox over Select when the option set is too long to scan
             (~10+) or the user may type a value that is not in it
             (allowsCustomValue). ComboBox is Input — the user TYPES and the
             list narrows; Select is Selection — picking from a closed set is
             the only act. Filtering matches the option's visible TEXT, not its
             id. Items are Selection/item (ADR-007 split, same as SelectItem).
Overlay:     Dialog, DialogModal, DialogTrigger, DialogHeading, DialogBody,
             DialogActions, Menu, MenuTrigger, ConfirmationDialog,
             Popover, PopoverTrigger, Tooltip, TooltipTrigger
             ActionMenu = THE OVERFLOW MENU (a row's trailing "…", a card's
             corner menu, the tail of a toolbar that ran out of room): composes
             MenuTrigger + icon-only ActionButton + Menu. aria-label is
             REQUIRED (no i18n runtime to default it — ADR-001); glyph is fixed
             to intent action.more; trigger evaluation defaults to secondary;
             forwards isOpen/defaultOpen/onOpenChange + children/items/
             disabledKeys/onAction/placement/offset/shouldFlip. Its meta is the
             TRIGGER (Action/root, data-scope="action-menu") — the surface keeps
             Menu's identity. This is a TOOLBAR's overflow answer; ButtonGroup's
             answer is collapsing its row to a column.
             MenuItem defaults to evaluation="muted" — a row shows NO fill until
             hovered (the quiet rung resolves to the popover's own colour). Pass
             another rung only to make one row louder. A destructive row uses
             consequence="destructive" (semantic marker, no colour);
             evaluation="negative" would fill the row red (F-029).
Feedback:    ProgressBar, Meter, Toast, ToastRegion, createToastQueue
             (Meter = static quantity in a range e.g. battery/disk;
             ProgressBar = a task in flight. Pick by "state" vs "progressing"),
             Badge (status chip, filled: evaluation=primary|positive|caution|negative|accent,
             numeric=tabular for counts — never a hand-rolled colored span)
Forms:       Form publishes field layout to every field inside it as STATIC
             context — necessityIndicator='icon'|'none' (default 'icon': an
             asterisk marks the REQUIRED fields, following the reference; 'none'
             drops it). Fields read it with a default, so a field outside any
             Form still marks itself required. Never put per-keystroke state in
             that context: every field reads it.
             The marker is aria-hidden — the control carries the native
             `required` attribute and no aria-required, so AT already announces
             it. CONSEQUENCE for tests: a required field's label textContent
             grows the asterisk, so getByLabelText('Email') with an exact string
             stops matching. Use getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' }) — it
             follows the accessible-name algorithm, which excludes the marker.
             Validation: React Aria's `native` default is right everywhere and
             needs no prop. Standalone, a `validate` callback and a malformed
             value each surface on blur; only `isRequired` waits for a submit,
             so a lone field needing a required check belongs in a Form (Form is
             the validation scope, not a synonym for a big form). Never pass
             validationBehavior="aria": it REMOVES native constraints.
             React Aria already focuses the first invalid field on submit.

Structure:   Form, FormActions, Wizard, WizardStep, WizardSummary,
             WizardNavigation, Separator, Group (labelled role=group frame),
             Toolbar (THE ACTION FAMILY'S UTILITY GROUP — the reference
             system's "ActionGroup"/ActionButtonGroup under the role's own name:
             role=toolbar, named region, arrow keys walk the controls.
             orientation=horizontal|vertical drives BOTH layout and the arrow-key
             axis; align=start|center|end. Hosts mixed controls (Select,
             ToggleButton, Separator) — the region and its keyboard model make it
             a toolbar, not the kind of control inside. Paints NOTHING: chrome is
             composed (Surface level=overlay + Toolbar for a floating bar), so
             there is no evaluation prop. Does NOT collapse like ButtonGroup — a
             toolbar that overflows moves its tail into an ActionMenu. Caveat: it
             is NOT a single tab stop, though APG's pattern asks for one —
             useToolbar cannot manage arbitrary children's tabindex (F-028)),
             Surface (depth container: level=flat|raised|overlay|blocking,
             padding=none|sm|md|lg; pairs the elevation shadow with the tonal
             surface colour so depth reads in light AND dark — use for cards,
             panels, sheets instead of a hand-rolled div),
             Heading (h1-h6 bound to the type scale: level=1..6 sets the
             element, size overrides the visual step — never a raw font-size),
             Text (copy + stat figures: variant=display-sm (stat step for KPI
             values/prices — data, not headings)|body|label-lg|md|sm, tone=muted for
             secondary hierarchy, as=p|span|div — never a raw font-size),
             Stack (layout rhythm: direction=vertical|horizontal picks the
             gap.stack|gap.inline family, gap=xs..xl, align, justify, wrap —
             never a raw gap; use instead of a hand-rolled flex div),
             ButtonGroup (the ACTION ROW: orientation=horizontal|vertical,
             align=start|center|end. Deliberately has NO gap prop — the
             separation between sibling actions is one product-wide decision, so
             every action row shares a rhythm; a Stack with a caller-picked gap
             is what it exists to replace. horizontal is ADAPTIVE: it measures
             and lays the actions out in a column when the row does not fit,
             publishing the rendered axis as data-orientation and marking a
             forced column data-collapsed="true"; orientation=vertical pins the
             column and skips the measurement. Grouped triggers stop shrinking
             (context, so it survives a Tooltip/DialogTrigger wrapper) — that is
             what makes the overflow measurable. Every action keeps its own tab
             stop: reach for Toolbar when the set should be ONE stop with
             arrow-key nav, DialogActions inside a Dialog (it reorders by
             composition per platform)),
             Box (token-constrained escape hatch, ADR-009: padding/
             paddingBlock/paddingInline=none|sm|md|lg, background=none|primary|
             muted, radius=none|control|surface|round, border=none|muted|
             strong, width=auto|full|fit, maxWidth=none|surface|reading —
             never a free style/className),
             Grid (2D layout: columns=N or minColumnWidth=xs|sm|md|lg for
             responsive auto-fit, rows, gap=xs..xl, align, justify — never a
             raw track template; each child gets a data-part="item" wrapper
             that is a size container, so theme cqi scales resolve to the
             track width),
             Container (centered page column: size=surface|reading,
             gutter=page|section|none — instead of max-width + margin auto;
             the column is a size container for theme cqi scales),
             AppShell (full-viewport app frame: header?, sidebar?, aside?,
             sidebarWidth/asideWidth=sm|md|lg, sidebarLabel/asideLabel for the
             landmark names; main content as children — instead of a
             hand-rolled viewport grid; every region is a size container for
             theme cqi scales),
             Code (code text: block=true scrollable <pre> surface, block=false
             inline <code> run)

Icons: Icon is a PUBLIC export (ADR-010): a semantic glyph named by intent
(`icon.{family}.{intent}`), never by picture — e.g.
<Icon intent="status.success" />, <Icon intent="action.close" size="sm" />.
Decorative by default (aria-hidden); pass `label` (caller-localized) only
when the icon is the sole carrier of meaning. Color inherits (currentColor);
size = sm|md|lg → vars.sizing.icon.*. Intents are a curated registry
(ICON_INTENTS): disclosure.expand/collapse, selection.checked/indeterminate,
action.close/search/increment/decrement/sortAscending/sortDescending,
status.success — it grows only on component/block demand. Glyphs map to
Lucide via the Iconify provider, registered offline (no runtime API fetch).

## Entity → token map (a component reads ONLY its row)

Action      → colors.action,        radii.action (pill in base), text.action (semibold),
            spacing.inset.action.block (block, 8-9px -> ~40px CTA) +
            spacing.inset.control.lg (inline), motion.feedback
Input       → colors.input,         radii.control, motion.feedback
Selection   → colors.input,         radii.control, motion.feedback
Navigation  → colors.navigation,    radii.control, motion.feedback
Disclosure  → colors.navigation,    radii.control, motion.transition
Overlay     → colors.informational, radii.surface, motion.transition, elevation.overlay
Feedback    → colors.feedback,      radii.surface (chips) / radii.round (rails), elevation.raised
Collection  → colors.informational, radii.surface
Structure   → colors.informational, radii.surface

Color path formula: `vars.colors.{ux}[evaluation][background|border|text][state]`
→ CSS var `--tt-colors-{ux}-{evaluation}-{dimension}-{state}`.

## Rules an integrating agent must follow

1. Composites accept NO `style`/`className`. Customize geometry via CSS
   custom-property knobs on the composite scope (fallbacks built in):
   `--fsl-dialog-max-width` (default min(500px, 90vw)),
   `--fsl-dialog-max-height` (90vh), `--fsl-menu-min-width` (12rem),
   `--fsl-menu-max-width` (min(320px, 90vw)),
   `--fsl-popover-max-width` (min(320px, 90vw)),
   `--fsl-tooltip-max-width` (min(280px, 90vw)).
   Example: `[data-scope='dialog'] { --fsl-dialog-max-width: 720px; }`
2. There is NO `size` prop anywhere. Different density = different
   semantic identity = different component.
3. i18n: flow-critical labels are REQUIRED props with no defaults —
   ConfirmationDialog (confirmLabel, cancelLabel, armedLabel when
   consequence="destructive") and WizardNavigation (prevLabel, nextLabel,
   finishLabel). Supply localized copy from the host app.
4. Validation: pass `isInvalid` (or React Aria `validate`) — never a color
   prop. Invalid styling comes from `input.*.{dimension}.invalid` tokens.
5. Destructive confirms: `<ConfirmationDialog consequence="destructive">`
   requires TWO clicks (arming). `consequence="committing"` +
   `evaluation="negative"` gives a red one-click confirm.
6. Every element exposes `data-scope`/`data-part` (plus `data-evaluation`,
   `data-consequence`, `data-composition`, `data-arming` where relevant) —
   use these for CSS targeting and tests; never rely on internal class names.
7. All layout is logical-property based (RTL-safe); keep host CSS logical too.

## Package facts

- ESM only, `sideEffects: false`, tree-shakes (Button-only import ≈ 1.8 KB
  min before deps). Peer deps: react >= 18, react-dom >= 18.
- `react-aria-components` pinned `~1.19.0` while Toast uses UNSTABLE_ APIs.
- SSR-safe: the only DOM injection (`@keyframes` for ProgressBar) happens in
  a client-only insertion effect. Icon glyphs register into an in-memory
  Iconify registry (no DOM, no network), so they are SSR-safe too.
- Icons: Iconify (`@iconify-icon/react`) is the official glyph provider;
  default set is Lucide (`@iconify/icons-lucide`, per-icon / tree-shakeable).
